I learned a lot of foundational knowledge through them, and the solid base I built there gives me the confidence to keep working in more complex domains.

parallel-programming-2026.title: Parallel Programming A Assignments
parallel-programming-2026.summary: A BUAA graduate Parallel Programming A repository for experiment problems, code, scripts, and run records.

images.ncuSharedMemory8192: NCU memory analysis for the shared-memory version
images.ncuSharedSource8192: NCU source-level analysis for the shared-memory version
images.ncuSharedWarpState8192: NCU warp state analysis for the shared-memory version

images.ncuNaiveO0Memory8192: NCU memory analysis for the naive O0 version
images.mpiMatrixProcessTimeline: MPI large-scale matrix multiplication process timeline
images.mpiMatrixTimeResult: MPI large-scale matrix multiplication timing result

projectIntro: **Connecting implementation with measurement**: Implemented naive and shared-memory CUDA GEMM, then used Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute to study memory access, warp states, and pipeline utilization and understand how implementation choices affect execution.

**Tracing source code to instructions**: Compared CUDA source, SASS, and measured instructions to analyze memory access, FMA, synchronization, and predicated execution. Studied access to kernel arguments, threadIdx, and blockIdx, and used instruction sequences to explain shared-memory and synchronization bottlenecks.
**Parallel programming practice**: Implemented and analyzed algorithms for typical course problems with OpenMP, pthread, and MPI.
**Reproducible experiments**: Organized code, helper scripts, and run records with C, Makefile, Shell, and Python so implementations and measurements can be revisited.

vr-raytracer-2026.title: Ray Tracing Renderer
vr-raytracer-2026.summary: A BUAA graduate Virtual Reality Integrated Experiment final project: a from-scratch C++ ray tracing renderer with JSON scenes, PPM/PNG output, mesh and material import, rendering reports, and Blender/CUDA exploration.

images.ncuGlassEmissiveSource: Nsight Compute source-level analysis for the emissive glass scene
images.blenderNsysTimeline16Spp: Nsight Systems timeline for a 16-sample Blender scene

projectIntro: **Standalone rendering system**: The team built a C++17 ray tracer from scratch, with JSON scene descriptions and PPM/PNG output.
**Scene and lighting support**: Provides sphere and triangle-mesh intersection, OBJ/GLB import, BVH acceleration, PBR, textures, transparent media, and emissive surfaces.
**Rendering validation**: Includes build scripts, regression tests, golden images, quality reports, and benchmarks for checking correctness and performance.
**Workflow extensions**: Explores a CUDA acceptance path and Blender RenderEngine integration to connect the standalone renderer with DCC workflows.
personalWork: **Toolchain integration and delivery**: Built Blender scenes and supported the plugin, local bridge, and remote rendering server, connecting the renderer with a Blender workflow.

**Performance diagnosis**: Used Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute to identify register pressure and local-memory spills in oversized CUDA kernels. Studied memory access and long scoreboard stalls to understand low efficiency, and documented the lack of shared, texture, and surface memory use.
**Image-quality improvement**: Integrated OIDN with albedo and normal auxiliary buffers to improve denoising and stability at low sample counts.
**Technical direction**: Proposed ray tracing as the team’s project direction based on my interest in rendering, graphics, and toolchain integration.

The implementation details are kept lightweight here; the emphasis is on Nsight Systems / Nsight Compute profiling, bottleneck observation, and multi-GPU performance analysis after the CUDA physical-animation work.

projectIntro: **Whole-program performance analysis**: Used Nsight Systems to separate initialization, data preparation, kernels, synchronization, and cleanup. Identified the kernel-active share of the full run and studied host/device and device/device transfers, event/stream coordination, and multi-GPU synchronization.

**Bottleneck assessment**: Used Nsight Compute to study kernel summaries and Roofline plots, assess compute versus memory limits, and compare stage-state construction, force computation, and RK4 weighted integration.

**Data layout and memory behavior**: Connected particle structures with Source Counters instructions to understand how AoS makes neighboring threads access non-contiguous addresses for the same component, lowering sector utilization, and examined the tool’s optimization suggestions.

**Dependencies and scheduling**: Connected Warp Stall distributions with source ordering and data dependencies to study long scoreboard, math pipe, barrier, and branch resolving stalls, and understand why few warps were eligible to issue.
**Hardware resource constraints**: Used occupancy charts to study how registers, per-block shared memory, block size, and residency limits jointly constrain theoretical occupancy.

**GPU simulation practice**: Implemented CUDA cloth and 3D SPH fluid simulation, used shared memory for neighborhood calculations, ran in a multi-GPU environment, and profiled kernels, memory access, and synchronization.

**Graphics workflow practice**: Built and rigged a quadruped in Blender, animated walking/running, and exported GLB, video, and presentation materials. Used the same model for an OpenGL/GLSL viewer, STL/OBJ/3DS parsing, textures, and Gouraud/Phong shading.
**Interactive deformation modeling**: Implemented mass-spring soft-tissue deformation on a brain model to observe local movement and recovery under mouse dragging.

os2023.title: MOS Operating System Labs
os2023.summary: Six BUAA Operating System labs covering paged memory, processes, IPC, exceptions, a file system, and a shell, with take-home coding and in-class implementation exams.

images.shellTimeRefill: Shell program timing with fast refill

projectIntro: **Low-level implementation and validation**: Implemented fast TLB refill for extra credit in MIPS assembly from CPU manuals and page-table layouts, without AI assistance. Used $k0/$k1 and coprocessor registers to reduce context-saving overhead, cutting runtime to about 25% of baseline under frequent TLB misses. Also found and fixed an ASID-reuse bug during testing.

**Root cause analysis across layers**: As a TA, investigated unexpected system behavior during syscall_write_dev writes to MALTA devices. Traced the issue to the OS-provided memcpy implementation and fixed it, supporting migration to QEMU and MIPS 4Kc.

**Source-level diagnosis and repair**: Investigated incomplete disk-block reclamation after file deletion, traced it to a block-counting error, fixed the calculation, and simplified redundant deletion logic.

**Building a system-level understanding**: Read nearly the entire OS codebase, including C, assembly, headers, Makefiles, and linker scripts. Revisited core call flows and kept extensive notes through questions and investigation.
**Technical teaching and documentation**: Delivered and recorded lab video lectures for a full course offering, maintained the lab OS, and answered student questions.
**Connecting software and hardware**: Used C and MIPS assembly on a GXemul-emulated MIPS R3000 to complete labs on paged memory, processes, IPC, exceptions, filesystems, and a shell.

parallel-programming-2024.title: Parallel Programming Coursework
parallel-programming-2024.summary: Undergraduate coursework at BUAA exploring process communication, thread synchronization, and parallel algorithms with MPI, Pthreads, and OpenMP. A CUDA final assignment built on Stanford's CS149 framework extends the work to GPU prefix sums and circle rendering. The repository preserves implementations, experiment data, reports, and algorithm diagrams.

images.circleRenderingComparison: Correct and incorrect CUDA circle rendering results for RGB and rand10K scenes
images.circleRenderingOptimizationResults: CUDA circle rendering: tile-based optimization and performance results
images.exclusivePrefixSumDiagram: Parallel exclusive prefix sum algorithm diagram
images.repeatedElementDetectionDiagram: Prefix-sum-based detection of adjacent repeated elements
images.scanAndRepeatPerformanceResults: Performance results for exclusive prefix sums and repeated-element detection

points: **Organizing parallel work**: Built a CUDA circle rasterizer within Stanford CS149 Assignment 3, using tile culling, shared memory, and prefix sums to organize relevant circles. Documented the design in reports and diagrams.

**GPU algorithm implementation**: Implemented SAXPY transfers, kernel execution, and timing in the same framework, along with parallel exclusive prefix sums and adjacent-repeat detection, preserving performance results.

**Comparing synchronization mechanisms**: Implemented Pthreads numerical integration with busy-wait, mutex, and semaphore reduction variants. Used condition variables to wake workers for task queues and linked-list operations.
**Distributed work partitioning**: Used MPI for Monte Carlo sampling and aggregation to estimate pi, and for parallel password enumeration with the course-provided MD5 library.
**Parallelization and evaluation**: Parallelized the course’s serial CYK reference implementation with OpenMP and recorded performance using timing scripts, experiment data, and a report.

compiler.title: SysY MIPS Compiler
compiler.summary: An independently built compiler for BUAA's Compiler Technology course, written in roughly 10,000 lines of Java. It compiles SysY through LLVM IR to 32-bit MIPS, supports arrays, recursion, and I/O, and combines semantic checks and basic optimizations with configurable output for inspecting each compilation stage.
points: **Language analysis and semantic modeling**: Built a lexer, recursive-descent parser, and AST for SysY, a C subset without pointer variables or floating-point types. Used hierarchical symbol tables for scope management, type checking, and error diagnostics.
**Control flow and intermediate representation**: Designed LLVM IR type and instruction representations, lowering array addressing, short-circuit evaluation, and control flow into IR for the backend.
**Target-code generation**: Wrote an LLVM IR-to-MIPS generator that manages stack frames, argument passing, and returns, supporting function calls and recursion on 32-bit MIPS.

**Basic optimization**: Implemented constant folding and local-variable access through immediate offsets from the stack pointer. Kept intermediate results in registers for subsequent operations and deferred writes to stack memory, saving values at register overwrites, jumps, and function calls as required.
**Inspectable compilation**: Added configurable diagnostics for nested syntax structures, live symbol tables, and generated code, making scope handling and code generation easier to inspect.
